tagline: Technology and data-driven leader in accessible and inclusive financial solutions
hero_kpi_rationale: E-commerce revenue represents a growing share of Rent-A-Center segment revenues (27% in 2025 vs 26% in 2024), reflecting the strategic importance of digital solutions in the rent-to-own business model.

kpis.name: E-commerce Revenue
kpis.explanation: Share of total revenue generated by online sales of the Rent-A-Center segment
kpis.description: E-commerce revenue represents a significant and growing share of total rent-to-own revenue of the Rent-A-Center segment

kpis.name: Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV)
kpis.explanation: Retail dollar value of merchandise acquired and leased by the Acima segment
kpis.description: GMV measures growth in new leases within the Acima segment, reflecting expansion of third-party retailer locations and productivity

kpis.name: Lease Portfolio Value
kpis.explanation: Aggregated dollar value of expected monthly lease revenue associated with active lease contracts
kpis.description: Represents the expected value of future lease revenues from company-owned Rent-A-Center stores and the e-commerce platform

kpis.name: Same Store Sales
kpis.explanation: Revenue from Rent-A-Center company-owned stores operated for at least 13 months, on a constant currency basis
kpis.description: Key performance indicator of established stores in the Rent-A-Center segment, excluding new acquisitions or relocations

kpis.name: Lease Charge-Offs (LCOs)
kpis.explanation: Write-off of net book value of uncollectible merchandise from customers in payment default
kpis.description: Key indicator of credit risk and quality of lease portfolios, expressed as a percentage of Rent-A-Center segment revenues

kpis.name: E-commerce Revenue Growth
kpis.explanation: Percentage point change in e-commerce revenue share of total Rent-A-Center revenue
kpis.description: Measures acceleration of digital transformation in the Rent-A-Center segment, reflecting shifts in consumer shopping behavior

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the past 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of $3.28B in the latest year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the past 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of $1.86B in the latest year

risks.title: Dependence on unfavorable macroeconomic conditions
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned first in the 'Risks Relating to Economic Conditions' section with intense language ('materially and adversely affect', 'significant impact'). The MD&A confirms that volatile macroeconomic conditions (inflation, interest rates, consumer behavior) had directly measurable impacts on 2025 results, particularly on the Rent-A-Center segment with a same-store-sales decline of 2.2%.

risks.title: Risks related to supply chain and distribution
risks.score_rationale: This risk is placed at the head of the 'Risks Relating to Our Vendors, Suppliers, Products and Services' section with strong language ('materially and adversely affect'). Supply chain disruptions and product cost increases are identified as factors affecting product availability and profitability of the rent-to-own business model.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party data and decision algorithms
risks.score_rationale: This risk is specifically documented for the entire company in 'Risks Relating to Our Vendors, Suppliers, Products and Services' with strong language ('material adverse effect'). The acquisition of Brigit strengthens this dependence: the company relies on external data for approval algorithms and advance disbursement. Inaccuracies or interruptions could seriously affect approval rates and portfolio losses.

risks.title: Increased regulatory and compliance risks
risks.score_rationale: This risk is placed at the head of the 'Risks Relating to Legal and Compliance Matters' section with very intense language ('significant monetary obligations', 'materially adverse'). Operated industries are heavily regulated (leasing, fintech, paycheck advances) with increased oversight. The acquisition of Brigit adds exposure to financial services regulations and earned wage access in multiple jurisdictions.

risks.title: Risks related to data security and privacy
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned in 'Risks Relating to Strategy and Operations' and 'Risks Relating to Legal and Compliance Matters' with strong language ('significant liability', 'damage our reputation'). The acquisition of Brigit substantially increases exposure: the platform manages personal financial data, salary information, and identity data from millions of customers.

risks.title: Credit and advance repayment risk (Brigit EWA)
risks.score_rationale: This risk is specifically detailed for the new Brigit segment in 'Risks Relating to Strategy and Operations' following the January 31, 2025 acquisition. The Earned Wage Access (EWA) segment is exposed to non-repayment risk if algorithm decision criteria are insufficient or data inaccurate. The 10-K explicitly defines 'Brigit Net Advance Losses' as a key metric.

risks.title: Integration and use of AI and similar technologies
risks.score_rationale: This risk is mentioned in 'Risks Relating to Strategy and Operations' with language indicating potential impact ('adversely affect our business, reputation, and results of operations'). The acquisition of Brigit strengthens this exposure: AI is integrated into approval algorithms, scoring models, and financial product recommendations. The risk remains moderate as it is presented as manageable through careful implementation.

ai_positioning.summary: UPBD is progressively integrating artificial intelligence and associated technologies into its operations. The acquisition of Brigit in January 2025 represents a strategic pivot toward financial health technologies and machine learning. The company acknowledges risks related to AI implementation but identifies this technology as critical to its future positioning as a leader in innovative financial solutions for underserved consumers.
evidence: Acquisition of Brigit (January 2025), a financial health technology company using decision algorithms and third-party data
Use of decision algorithms for customer approval and advance disbursement
Dependence on third-party data for automated decision models
Explicit mention of AI integration risks in 'Risks Relating to Strategy and Operations'
